title: Bikini Wax vs. Brazilian Wax: Types, Coverage, and How to Choose
summary: Learn the difference between a bikini and a Brazilian wax: where they remove hair, which is most uncomfortable, and what to choose for your first time.
body_markdown:
Ever wondered about the difference between a bikini wax and a Brazilian wax? If so, you’re not alone. “Bikini waxing” is often used as a catch-all to describe any type of pubic hair waxing, so it’s easy to see why the two get confused.


Here, we’ll cover the different types of bikini waxing, everything that’s included in a Brazilian wax, and how to choose the right option—especially if it’s your first time.


**Bikini Line Wax** **Full Bikini Wax** **Brazilian Wax**


Hair removed Along the top and sides of the bikini area All or some hair from the front, including the labia All or some hair from the front, plus between the buttocks


Customizable? No, focuses on edges Yes, leave as much or as little hair as you'd like Yes, leave as much or as little hair as you'd like


Butt strip included? No No Yes


Discomfort level Least painful More uncomfortable -- sensitive areas included More uncomfortable --sensitive areas included (same as full bikini)


Best for Cleaning up bikini line More thorough hair removal without butt strip Most comprehensive hair removal


## What is the difference between a bikini wax and a Brazilian wax?


The main difference between a


[bikini wax and a Brazilian wax](https://waxcenter.com/pages/brazilian-waxing) is how much hair is removed and from where. A bikini line wax cleans up the edges, while a full bikini wax and Brazilian wax offer more comprehensive hair removal. The key difference? A Brazilian also includes a butt strip.


## What is a bikini wax?


A bikini wax removes hair from the pubic area. At European Wax Center, we offer two types of bikini waxing to help you customize your results: a bikini line wax and a full bikini wax.


### What is a bikini line wax?


A bikini line wax removes hair along the top and sides of your bikini area, following where the edges of your swimwear or underwear typically sit. It’s a simple way to keep the area neatly groomed without removing much hair.


### What is a full bikini wax?


A full bikini wax goes beyond the edges of your bikini line to remove all hair from the front of the pubic area, including the labia. Prefer to leave some hair? You can keep a strip, triangle, square, or any amount you like. It's entirely up to you.


## What is a Brazilian wax?


A


[Brazilian wax](https://waxcenter.com/pages/brazilian-waxing-what-to-expect) includes full pubic hair removal as well as a strip between the buttocks (also known as a butt strip). Like a full bikini wax, you can choose to leave some hair in the front or remove it all.


At European Wax Center, we’ve performed over 5 million Brazilian waxes. You could say it’s kind of our thing. With over 20 years of experience, we’ve refined every detail—from specialized waxing techniques and application patterns to the rigorous training our Wax Specialists receive. The result? Expert care and consistently smooth results, every time.


## What to expect from a bikini wax?


Whether you opt for a bikini line wax, full bikini wax, or a Brazilian, you can expect a similar process. Once you’re in the waxing suite,


[your service will take 15-30 minutes](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/how-long-does-a-brazilian-wax-take) . At EWC, we use a signature


[4-step waxing method](https://waxcenter.com/pages/first-wax-advice) designed to maximize your comfort while ensuring smooth results that make you feel confident.


1.


Cleanse


. A quick cleanse helps remove oils and other impurities that could interfere with the wax.


2.


Protect.


A pre-wax oil is applied to create a protective barrier over your skin.


3.


Wax.


Your Wax Specialist applies our Comfort Wax® using techniques tailored to your hair type and growth patterns.


4.


Rejuvenate.


A post-wax serum is applied to soothe skin and help prevent ingrown hairs.


## Does a bikini wax hurt more than a Brazilian?


A bikini wax isn't necessarily more or less painful than a Brazilian wax. The level of discomfort depends on the type of bikini wax you choose and your individual pain tolerance.


A bikini line wax is generally the least uncomfortable option because it removes hair along the outer edges of the pubic area, which tend to be less sensitive.


A full bikini wax and a Brazilian wax both involve removing hair from the front of the pubic area, including the labia, so you can expect similar sensations. The main difference is that a Brazilian also includes a butt strip, which most guests find to be one of the easiest parts of the service.

so it’s tough on unwanted hair—not on your skin.


Don’t forget to check out our


[guide to a more comfortable wax](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/how-to-make-waxing-more-comfortable-a-guide-to-a-more-comfortable-wax) .


## How long does a bikini wax last?


Whether you choose a bikini wax or a Brazilian, the results typically last 3–4 weeks. This timeframe can vary a bit from person to person, depending on your hair type and how quickly it grows. For your next wax, hair needs to be at least ¼ inch long (about the length of a grain of rice). Most people find that waxing every 3–4 weeks gives their hair enough time to reach the ideal length.


H2: How should I prepare for a bikini wax?


A little


[pre-wax preparation](https://waxcenter.com/pages/first-wax-prep) will help you get the best results from your bikini or Brazilian wax. Here's what we recommend before your reservation:


-


Let your hair grow.


Hair should be at least ¼ inch long (about the length of a grain of rice) so the wax has enough to grip.


-


Exfoliate ahead of time.


Gently exfoliate 2–3 days before your wax to remove dead skin cells.


-


Keep skin clean and product-free.


Skip lotions, oils, and other products on the day of your wax.


-


Dress comfortably.


Wear loose, breathable clothing to minimize friction against freshly waxed skin.


For more tips on what to do (and what to avoid) before your reservation, check out our


[bikini waxing dos and don’ts](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/our-top-6-dos-donts-of-bikini-waxing) .


## Which bikini wax should I start with as a first-timer?


Which bikini wax you choose for


[your first time waxing](https://waxcenter.com/pages/first-wax-advice) depends on how much hair you'd like to remove and what feels comfortable for you. There's no right or wrong place to start.


If you're concerned about discomfort or have a lower pain tolerance, a bikini line wax is a great way to ease in. It focuses on the outer edges of the pubic area, which are typically less sensitive, and gives you a chance to get familiar with the experience.


If you're ready for more hair removal, there's no reason you can't start with a full bikini or Brazilian wax. Both give you the flexibility to remove as much or as little hair as you'd like from the front. The only difference is that a Brazilian also includes a butt strip, which many guests find to be the easiest part of the service.
